name: Confidence Indicator
summary: Communicate model certainty levels in text or structured output, from high confidence to uncertainty to refusal, so users know how much to trust the response.
problem: Model responses arrive without metadata about how reliable they are. Users cannot distinguish between high-confidence answers and best-guess speculation, leading to misplaced trust in unreliable output or unwarranted skepticism of good answers.
useWhen: The model can express different levels of certainty about its output
Users need to weight the response confidence against the stakes of their decision
The output mixes factual retrieval with extrapolation or reasoning
dontUseWhen: The model cannot articulate its own uncertainty (no confidence or reasoning metadata available)
All outputs are equally trusted or equally distrusted by design
Displaying uncertainty would create unwarranted anxiety without actionable recourse

anatomy.description: The visual element (icon, badge, color, meter) that represents confidence level.
The text label or aria-label that describes the confidence level in plain language.
Optional section that users can expand to see why the model expressed this confidence level.
If confidence is low or conditional, the space where limitations or caveats are displayed.

states.description: The model is highly confident in the response.
The model has moderate confidence; the answer is plausible but not certain.
The model is uncertain and signals this explicitly.
The model's confidence depends on unstated assumptions; caveat region is populated.
The model declined to answer; reason is provided.

constraints.statement: The confidence indicator MUST represent the model's actual confidence without overstating it; calibration toward uncertainty is safer than toward false certainty.
constraints.rationale: Miscalibrated confidence (showing high when actual is low) erodes user trust permanently once discovered; the cost of false negatives (low when high) is lower.
constraints.verification: Human review comparing model's stated confidence against ground truth for a representative sample.

constraints.statement: Confidence level MUST be communicated via text label or aria-label, not color or icon alone.
constraints.rationale: Color-blind and screen reader users cannot perceive confidence from visual cues alone.
constraints.verification: Unit test asserting the indicator element has aria-label or accessible text content matching confidence level.

constraints.statement: If an expandable detail region exists, it MUST be keyboard-accessible and focusable.
constraints.rationale: Keyboard and assistive technology users must be able to reach and interact with caveats and reasoning.
constraints.verification: E2E test: Tab to the expandable region and verify it can be opened via Enter or Space.

constraints.statement: In the refusal state, the reason for refusal SHOULD be displayed alongside the refusal indicator.
constraints.rationale: Users are less frustrated by refusal when they understand why; transparency reduces perceived arbitrariness.
constraints.verification: Manual review: verify that refusal states include an explanation of why the model declined.

constraints.statement: Confidence levels SHOULD be labeled in plain language (e.g., 'likely', 'uncertain', 'can't determine') rather than numerical scores or model-internal concepts.
constraints.rationale: Users do not calibrate on confidence scores; plain language is more actionable and universally understood.
constraints.verification: Code review: verify that confidence labels in the component use plain language, not numeric or jargon terms.

constraints.statement: Confidence labels MUST be consistent throughout the UI; the same term always means the same confidence level.
constraints.rationale: Inconsistent terminology leads users to misinterpret confidence, undermining the entire pattern.
constraints.verification: Unit test: verify that a mapping of labels to confidence levels exists and is applied uniformly.

wcagCriteria.name: Contrast (Minimum)
wcagCriteria.relevance: If confidence is indicated by color alone, contrast must meet WCAG AA for distinguishability.

wcagCriteria.name: Non-text Contrast
wcagCriteria.relevance: Icons representing confidence levels must have sufficient contrast.

wcagCriteria.name: Name, Role, Value
wcagCriteria.relevance: Confidence indicators and any expandable regions must have accessible names and roles.

keyboard.action: Reaches the confidence indicator and any expandable details in document order.
Toggles the expandable detail region if present.

screenReader.behavior: Screen reader announces the confidence level (e.g., 'high confidence') and whether details are available.
Screen reader announces the region as expanded and reads the caveat or reasoning.

accessibility.focusManagement: Focus is never stolen by the indicator itself; expandable regions are keyboard-accessible in natural tab order.
accessibility.reducedMotion: Expand/collapse animations are disabled under prefers-reduced-motion; regions appear and disappear instantly.

do: Place the indicator near the output it qualifies, not separated in a sidebar.
Use icon + label combinations so color is never the only signal.
Pair uncertainty with actionable next steps: 'uncertain — try rephrasing your prompt' or 'uncertain — regenerate'
dont: Do not use numerical confidence scores (0–100) without translating them to plain language.
Do not hide low confidence in a collapsed region; lead with it so users see the caveat immediately.
Do not use generic 'learn more' links; explain *what* makes the answer uncertain.

references.title: Calibration of Confidence
references.note: Understanding why model calibration matters for user trust.
